3349-the-wandering-jew-volume-11.title: The Wandering Jew Volume 11
3349-the-wandering-jew-volume-11.creator: Eugene Sue
3349-the-wandering-jew-volume-11.description: A book by Eugene Sue. Suddenly, through the shadow thrown by the overhanging wood, which stretches far into endless depths, a human form appears. She advances slowly towards the ruins. She treads the once sacred ground. This woman is pale, her look sad, her long robe floats on the wind, her feet covered with dust. She walks with difficulty and pain.

arxiv-2012-10433.title: Drop Impact Dynamics of Complex Fluids: A Review
arxiv-2012-10433.creator: Phalguni Shah, Michelle M. Driscoll
arxiv-2012-10433.description: Abstract The impact of fluid drops on solid substrates has widespread interest in many industrial coating and spraying applications, such as ink-jet printing and agricultural pesticide sprays. Many of the fluids used in these applications are non-Newtonian, that is they contain particulate or polymeric additives that strongly modify their flow behaviour.

arxiv-2108-13748.title: Local large deviations for periodic infinite horizon Lorentz gases
arxiv-2108-13748.creator: Ian Melbourne, Françoise Pène, Dalia Terhesiu
arxiv-2108-13748.description:
A 2021 arXiv research paper by Ian Melbourne, Françoise Pène, Dalia Terhesiu. We prove local large deviations for the periodic infinite horizon Lorentz gas viewed as a ℤ d \mathbb{Z}^{d} -cover ( d = 1 , 2 d=1,2 ) of a dispersing billiard. arxiv-2202-01711.title: Algorithmic Fairness Datasets: the Story so Far
arxiv-2202-01711.creator: Alessandro Fabris, Stefano Messina, Gianmaria Silvello, Gian Antonio Susto
arxiv-2202-01711.description: Abstract Data-driven algorithms are studied and deployed in diverse domains to support critical decisions, directly impacting people’s well-being. As a result, a growing community of researchers has been investigating the equity of existing algorithms and proposing novel ones, advancing the understanding of risks and opportunities of automated decision-making for historically disadvantaged populations.

arxiv-2203-03293.title: Neural network approach to reconstructing spectral functions and complex poles of confined particles Journal: SciPost Physics. The published version is available at doi:10.21468/SciPostPhys.13.4.097
arxiv-2203-03293.creator: Thibault Lechien, David Dudal
arxiv-2203-03293.description: Abstract Reconstructing spectral functions from propagator data is difficult as solving the analytic continuation problem or applying an inverse integral transformation are ill-conditioned problems. Recent work has proposed using neural networks to solve this problem and has shown promising results, either matching or improving upon the performance of other methods.

arxiv-2204-00938.title: Two-sided cartesian fibrations of synthetic ( ∞ , 1 ) (\infty,1) -categories
arxiv-2204-00938.creator: Jonathan Weinberger
arxiv-2204-00938.description: Abstract . Within the framework of Riehl–Shulman’s synthetic ( ∞ , 1 ) (\infty,1) -category theory, we present a theory of two-sided cartesian fibrations. Central results are several characterizations of the two-sidedness condition à la Chevalley, Gray, Street, and Riehl–Verity, a two-sided Yoneda Lemma, as well as the proof of several closure properties.

arxiv-2207-05022.title: STI: Turbocharge NLP Inference at the Edge via Elastic Pipelining DOI: 10.1145/3575693.3575698 asplosb23main-p32-p ISBN: 978-1-4503-9916-6/23/03 Conference: Proceedings of the 28th ACM International Conference on Architectural Support for Programming Languages and Operating Systems, Volume 2; March
arxiv-2207-05022.creator: Liwei Guo, Wonkyo Choe, Felix Xiaozhu Lin
arxiv-2207-05022.description: Abstract . Natural Language Processing (NLP) inference is seeing increasing adoption by mobile applications, where on-device inference is desirable for crucially preserving user data privacy and avoiding network roundtrips. Yet, the unprecedented size of an NLP model stresses both latency and memory, creating a tension between the two key resources of a mobile device.

arxiv-2311-15805.title: Massless fermions and superconductivity of string-wall composites
arxiv-2311-15805.creator: Minoru Eto, and Yuito Suzuki
arxiv-2311-15805.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Minoru Eto, and Yuito Suzuki. An axion cosmic string is known to be a chiral superconductor when the axion couples to an electrically charged fermion. After the QCD phase transition, a QCD axion string is attached by N N domain walls. We would like to elucidate the fate of massless fermions on a global string after domain walls attached not only in the axion model but also in general models having string-wall composites.

arxiv-2501-04873.title: Back Home: A Machine Learning Approach to Seashell Classification and Ecosystem Restoration
arxiv-2501-04873.description: Abstract In Costa Rica, an average of 5 tons of seashells are extracted from ecosystems annually. Confiscated seashells, cannot be returned to their ecosystems due to the lack of origin recognition. To address this issue, we developed a convolutional neural network (CNN) specifically for seashell identification.

arxiv-2505-07003.title: CMD: Controllable Multiview Diffusion for 3D Editing and Progressive Generation
arxiv-2505-07003.creator: Peng Li, Suizhi Ma, Jialiang Chen, Yuan Liu, Congyi Zhang, Wei Xue, Wenhan Luo, Alla Sheffer, Wenping Wang, Yike Guo
arxiv-2505-07003.description: Abstract . Recently, 3D generation methods have shown their powerful ability to automate 3D model creation. However, most 3D generation methods only rely on an input image or a text prompt to generate a 3D model, which lacks the control of each component of the generated 3D model.

arxiv-2507-14647.title: Multi-Sampling-Frequency Naturalness MOS Prediction Using Self-Supervised Learning Model with Sampling-Frequency-Independent Layer
arxiv-2507-14647.creator: Go Nishikawa 1∗ , Wataru Nakata 1∗ , Yuki Saito 1,2 , Kanami Imamura 1,2 , Hiroshi Saruwatari 1 , and Tomohiko Nakamura 2
arxiv-2507-14647.description: Abstract We introduce our submission to the AudioMOS Challenge (AMC) 2025 Track 3: mean opinion score (MOS) prediction for speech with multiple sampling frequencies (SFs). Our submitted model integrates an SF-independent (SFI) convolutional layer into a self-supervised learning (SSL) model to achieve SFI speech feature extraction for MOS prediction.

europmc-pmc6827047.description: The mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathway is an important bridge in the switch from extracellular signals to intracellular responses. Alterations of signaling cascades are found in various diseases, including cancer, as a result of genetic and epigenetic changes....

pmc-10605560.title: miRNA Associated With Glucose Transporters in Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma: A Systematic Review
pmc-10605560.creator: Priyadharshini R, Monal Yuwanati, Saravanan Sekaran, Senthilmurugan M
pmc-10605560.description: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) is a malignancy of the oral cavity with poor prognosis. Dysregulation in glycolytic pathways involving glucose transporters (GLUT) has been implicated in poor prognosis. Furthermore, GLUT expression in cancer cells is regulated by several miRNAs. However, there is a lack of data about miRNA involved in the regulation of GLUT in OSCC.

pmc-12382076.title: Identification of a novel POU4F3 frameshift variant in a Chinese family with autosomal dominant hearing loss
pmc-12382076.creator: Jie Li, Shengmei Yang, Zonghui Feng, Xueshuang Huang, Genyun Tang, Youya Niu, Yunqi Yang, Bin Wang, Haiou Jiang
pmc-12382076.description: BackgroundAutosomal dominant nonsyndromic hearing loss (ADNSHL) is characterised by highly clinical and genetic heterogeneity. A variant of POU4F3 is considered the pathogenic cause of ADNSHL, specifically designated as autosomal dominant nonsyndromic deafness 15 (DFNA15). The aim of this study was to explore the genetic variants and molecular pathogenic mechanism for a Chinese pedigree with DFNA15.

pmc-12599001.title: Predictive value of stress hyperglycaemia ratio for 28-day all-cause mortality in elderly patients with hip fracture: a retrospective single-centre study in Beijing Jishuitan Hospital, Capital Medical University, Beijing, China

pmc-12744913.title: When the Ileum Mimics Appendicitis: A Case of Uncomplicated Ileal Diverticulitis
pmc-12744913.creator: Hanane Aksim, Bah Alpha Amadou, Oualid Haddadia, Meryem Belhamdiya, Rachid Akka
pmc-12744913.description: Although colonic and duodenal diverticulosis is common, ileal diverticular disease is rare. The pathophysiology of ileal diverticula is poorly understood, but the most widely accepted hypothesis currently suggests abnormalities in the myenteric plexus or smooth muscle, high intraluminal pressure, and intestinal dyskinesia.

pmc-13051191.title: Evaluating the Efficacy of a Novel Triangle Suture Technique in Scleral-Fixation of Intraocular Lens
pmc-13051191.creator: Or Shmueli, Nir Erdinest, Salome Goldmann, Yossi Eshel, Aseel Gebara, Ori Saban, Samer Khateb, Edward Averbukh, Itay Lavy
pmc-13051191.description: PurposeThe study aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of a novel Triangle Suture Technique in the surgical placement of Scleral-Fixated Intraocular Lenses (SFIOLs). The research seeks to address the challenges in cases associated with inadequate capsular support for Intraocular Lens (IOL) implantation, offering an alternative to traditional methods.

pmc-13320590.creator: Zeyu Wu, Mengting Lu, Lei Xu, Ming Luo, Limei Shan, Hongxia Xing, Wenwen Li, Junling Qian

pmc-13450893.title: Heuristic rules for cooperative transport in wood ant nest maintenance
pmc-13450893.creator: Natalie Arscott, Cornelia Buehlmann, Andrew Philippides, Paul Graham
pmc-13450893.description: Collective behaviour in ants includes cooperative transport where individuals control behaviour relative to an object. Some species show efficient collective food transport because individuals share directional information. It is less clear how individuals coordinate in tasks, such as movement of nest material, where movement direction is unclear. Wood ants build nests from twigs and leaf litter that require constant maintenance.

pmc-13458707.title: Context-dependent interplay of Swi-Snf and Tup1-Cyc8 influences chromatin and transcription at antagonistically regulated genes
pmc-13458707.creator: Xuyuan Guo, Mohamed M Alhussain, Brenda Lee, Nicole Byrne, Karsten Hokamp, Hadel Aljaeed, Reham H Alnajjar, Zain M F Baazeem, Georgina Smethurst, Carsten Kröger, Charles A S Banks, Michael C Church, Jerry L Workman, Nicholas A Kent, Alastair B Fleming
pmc-13458707.description: The yeast Swi-Snf co-activator was the first chromatin remodelling complex discovered which can disrupt promoter nucleosomes to enable transcription. The Tup1-Cyc8 complex was the first global co-repressor identified which can position nucleosomes across promoters to block transcription. However, the global extent of their antagonistic regulation of gene transcription in yeast is unknown.
